06 LoudnessEBUR128

Essentia reference ↗

All loudness values are based on the Loudness Units Full Scale (LUFS). THE LUFS scale quantifies the perceived loudness of a sound by mimicking human hearing. Values range from -70 to 0, with values closer to 0 indicating a louder sound.

LoudnessEBUR128 variables
NameTypeValuesDescription
Loudness_ebu128_integrated#number−70–0 LUFSThe overall loudness of a song.
Loudness_ebu128_loudness_range#numberReal numberThe loudness range over an arbitrary long time interval. Computed from short-term (3 second windows) loudness values, the loudness range is the difference between the 95th percentile and 10th percentile loudness values.Also listed as: Loudness_ebu128_loundess_range
Calculation note

From audio frames to song-level features

All songs are at 44.1kHz. Spectral, dissonance, and MFCC values are calculated via frames. Frames are composed of 2048 samples, approximately 46.44ms at 44.1Khz. Therefore, a song contains thousands of frames, and each frame has its own spectral, dissonance, and MFCC values calculated. These values are averaged for each song, allowing for easier interpretability and comparison.

11 MFCC

Essentia reference ↗

MFCC’s refer to the mel frequency cepstrum coefficients, which describes the timbre of a song. To calculate the coefficients, the function uses a filterbank of 40 bands from 0 to 11000Hz, takes the log value of the spectrum energy in each mel band (a specific frequency range that mimics the human ear), and transforms the 40 bands to 13 mel coefficients through discrete cosine transformation (DCT). MFCC_mean_# refer to the average mel frequency cepstrum coefficients across the entire song. Coefficients 1-3 represents the overall spectral envelope of the song, while coefficients 4-13 capture specific spectral details, with coefficient 13 containing the most fine-grained details. Interpretations of these coefficients are impracticable, but they are useful in machine learning.

About these definitions

Variable descriptions are reproduced as supplied by the project author. All songs are at 44.1kHz. The shared Excel workbook filename and worksheet are awaiting confirmation.

The current charts use chart-ranking data. Links to charts using these audio features will appear on variable names as those charts are added. The # beside each name links directly to its dictionary entry.

Dictionary structure inspired by the tidyverse elevators example ↗. Algorithm references accompany each feature group.
